changed: dashboard Storage tab with cache breakdown and top directories
summary: Each discovered worktree now has a persistent disk-usage snapshot covering total allocated bytes, .next, .next/cache, node_modules, other files, and the five largest top-level directories. The dashboard presents all worktrees in a dedicated Storage tab with manual refresh and a bounded total-versus-.next history chart.

Filesystem scans run one at a time, never follow symlinks, and are automatically scheduled only for missing or six-hour-old dashboard data. MCP exposes the cached snapshots through a read-only tool and does not initiate expensive scans.
title: Shipped worktree disk and cache visibility
validation: Scanner tests cover known cache categories, top-level ranking, and a symlink to an external directory that must not contribute to the result.
Storage-manager and SQLite tests cover global scan serialization, persistence, latest breakdown, and the 180-sample history bound.
HTTP and MCP tests cover explicit worktree refresh validation boundaries and read-only storage results.
